searches.reason: Test whether weak separation comes from the training objective rather than recurrent memory. Compare one practical loss or sampling intervention against the corrected GRU4Rec baseline; Electronics motivates this direction, but selection must use four-category macro validation HR@10. Negatives must use training data only, and inference must retain one model per category.

searches.reason: Explore whether one jointly trained GRU can preserve persistent preferences while responding to recent coherent activity. Seek recurrent mechanisms beyond the previous scalar retention gate, with controlled comparisons that distinguish useful memory from simple recency weighting. Preserve causal inputs, padding-safe updates and final-nonpadding readout.
searches.query: GRU sequential recommendation 2023–2026 multi-timescale recurrent memory adaptive interest persistence session boundary latent intent

searches.reason: Investigate whether titles and descriptions can improve distinctions between superficially related items inside a single GRU-based network. Favor lightweight text encoders trained from scratch and joint next-item or contrastive objectives; exclude pretrained weights, unavailable attributes and separately fitted semantic scores. Text similarity alone cannot establish compatibility or current need.
searches.query: content-aware GRU sequential recommendation 2023–2026 jointly learned item text encoder titles descriptions semantic hard negatives without pretrained models
